(Boundary Increase) | nrhp_type = hd | image = Van Vorst Park Jersey City November 2021.jpg | caption = | location = Roughly bounded by Mercer, Wayne, Montgomery, Grove, Bright, Varick and Monmouth Streets, [[Jersey City, New Jersey]] | coordinates = {{coord|40|43|7|N|74|2|53|W|display=inline}} | pushpin_map = USA New Jersey Hudson County#New Jersey#USA | nocat = yes | architect = | architecture = Late 19th And 20th Century Revivals | added = October 11, 1984 | area = {{convert|7.7|acre}} | ref_num = 84000084{{NRISref|2009a}} | designated_other1_name = New Jersey Register of Historic Places | designated_other1_abbr = NJRHP | designated_other1_link = New Jersey Register of Historic Places | designated_other1_date = August 2, 1978 | designated_other1_number = 1540{{cite web | title=New Jersey and National Registers of Historic Places - Hudson County | url=http://www.state.nj.us/dep/hpo/1identify/lists/hudson.pdf | publisher=[[New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection]] - Historic Preservation Office | page=7 | date=July 7, 2009 | access-date=August 3, 2010}} | designated_other1_num_position = bottom | designated_other1_color = #ffc94b }} '''Van Vorst Park''' is a neighborhood in the [[Downtown Jersey City|Historic Downtown]] of [[Jersey City, New Jersey|Jersey City]], [[Hudson County, New Jersey|Hudson County]], [[New Jersey]], centered on a park sharing the same name. The neighborhood is located west of [[Paulus Hook]] and Marin Boulevard, north of Grand Street, east of the [[Interstate 78 in New Jersey|Turnpike Extension]], and south of [[The Village, Jersey City|The Village]] and Christopher Columbus Drive. Much of it is included in the Van Vorst Park Historical District.*[http://www.cityofjerseycity.org/docs/vanvorst.shtml Van Vorst Park Historical District] The park was a centerpiece of [[Van Vorst Township, New Jersey|Van Vorst Township]], a [[township (New Jersey)|township]] that existed in Hudson County from 1841 to 1851. Van Vorst was incorporated as a township by an Act of the [[New Jersey Legislature]] on April 12, 1841, from portions of [[Bergen Township, New Jersey (pre-1862)|Bergen Township]]. On March 18, 1851, Van Vorst Township was annexed by [[Jersey City, New Jersey|Jersey City]].Snyder, John P. [https://www.state.nj.us/dep/njgs/enviroed/oldpubs/bulletin67.pdf ''The Story of New Jersey's Civil Boundaries: 1606-1968''], Bureau of Geology and Topography; Trenton, New Jersey; 1969. p. 148. Accessed June 26, 2013. The name Van Vorst comes from a prominent family in the area, the first of which arrived in the 1630s as superintendent of the [[patroonship]] [[Pavonia, New Netherland|Pavonia]], the earliest European settlement on the west bank of the [[Hudson River]] in the province of [[New Netherland]]. His homestead at [[Harsimus]], plus others at [[Communipaw]], [[Paulus Hook]], [[Greenville, Jersey City|Minakwa]], [[Pamrapo]] were later incorporated into [[Bergen, New Netherland|Bergen]]. His namesake and eighth generation descendant, [[Cornelius Van Vorst]], was the twelfth [[List of mayors of Jersey City|Mayor of Jersey City]] serving from 1860 to 1862.{{Cite web|url=https://njcu.libguides.com/vanvorstpark|title=Library Guides: Van Vorst Park: Van Vorst Park}}{{Cite web|url=https://njcu.libguides.com/vanvorst1|title=Library Guides: Van Vorst Homestead Site: Van Vorst Homestead Site}} Like [[Harsimus]] Cove and [[Hamilton Park, Jersey City|Hamilton Park]] to the north and [[Bergen-Lafayette, Jersey City|Bergen-Lafayette]] to the southwest, the neighborhood contains nineteenth century [[rowhouse]]s and [[brownstone]]s.[http://www.newyorkssixth.com/directory/labels/Neighborhood%20Profile.html Hamilton Park Neighborhood and Historic District] It is home to the [[Jersey City Free Public Library]], [[James J. Ferris High School]] (named for the Jersey City citizen who laid the foundation of the [[Hudson and Manhattan Railroad Powerhouse]] with his firm Stillman, Delehanty and Ferris),{{Cite web |url=http://www.jclandmarks.org/campaign-powerhouse.shtml |title=JERSEY CITY POWERHOUSE TO UNDERGO FIRST PHASE OF LONG-AWAITED RESTORATION |access-date=January 24, 2010 |archive-date=June 17, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130617114127/http://jclandmarks.org/campaign-powerhouse.shtml |url-status=dead }}[http://www.jclandmarks.org/nomination-embankment.shtml The Pennsylvania Railroad Harsimus Branch Embankment, Jersey City, NJ] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090523092253/http://www.jclandmarks.org/nomination-embankment.shtml |date=2009-05-23 }} and Old Colony Shopping Plaza. Landmarks include [[Barrow Mansion]] and [[Dixon Mills]]. The [[Grove Street (PATH station)|Grove Street PATH station]] is located nearby to the north, and so is the [[Jersey Avenue (HBLR station)]] to the south. == Park == [[File:Gazebo in Van Vorst Park.jpg|thumb|upright=1.1|Gazebo in Van Vorst Park]] Van Vorst Park is a two-acre city park bounded by Barrow Street to the east, Montgomery Street to the north, Jersey Avenue to the west, and York Street to the south. The park was renovated in 1999 at a cost of $2 million, with money raised by the Friends of Van Vorst Park.{{cite web|title=Jersey City, Past and
